picks.title: Natsume Yuujinchou
picks.case: You gave Mushishi a 9, and this is the other great episodic show about a quiet person walking into someone else's small supernatural problem and leaving it a little better. It has the same structure Mushishi does, one self-contained visit per episode, with the emotional weight carried by the people rather than the spirits. If what you liked about Sousou no Frieren was the long, patient accumulation of small farewells, Natsume does that too.

picks.title: Houseki no Kuni
picks.case: Sousou no Frieren is a 10 on your list and this shares its real subject, which is what centuries do to somebody who cannot die. It is a fantasy adventure on the surface and a slow, unsparing character study underneath, the same trick Shouwa Genroku Rakugo Shinjuu pulls with a much smaller cast. The CGI is a genuine stylistic choice here rather than a budget one.

picks.title: Sonny Boy
picks.case: You scored Ping Pong the Animation an 8, so you can clearly sit with a show that trusts its visual language over its dialogue. Sonny Boy is the most formally adventurous series on this list and it uses that freedom to ask what a group of teenagers owes each other. It is twelve episodes and it does not explain itself, which is the same deal Ping Pong offered.

picks.title: Kusuriya no Hitorigoto
picks.case: This is the closest thing airing now to Shouwa Genroku Rakugo Shinjuu, a period drama that cares more about institutions and grudges than about spectacle. The mysteries are small and pharmacological rather than violent, which should suit somebody who rated Mushishi a 9. It is also currently airing, so you would be watching it week to week alongside Dungeon Meshi.
